minutes.headline: Task force chose to pursue a consultant for the street light LED grant and set a March 15 deadline for departments' project info.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force approved earlier minutes, then spoke with a state Green Communities staffer about the next competitive grant application, focusing on a street light LED conversion with a consultant and installer. Members worked out rough consultant cost estimates from MAPC contract rates and discussed other possible projects and wireless light monitoring. No formal votes beyond the minutes; the chair will contact MAPC, ask Heather about procurement, and write to departments for project data.

attendees.role: presenter (state Green Communities staff, joined remotely)

votes.motion: Approve the prior meeting minutes (December minutes)
votes.outcome: passed (ayes have it, count not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: The state staffer said the cap for the next grant round is a set maximum, and a purchase price need not be in hand but must be shown in process.
A prior unsolicited bid from the vendor was a rough number for the street light conversion; the chair said it needs updating.
The 2017 total retrofit estimate was shown on screen; members expect lighting costs may be lower but labor higher now.

budget_items.topic: Consultant cost estimate from MAPC unit rates
budget_items.what_was_said: Using per-fixture rates in the MAPC decision summary, the chair computed consultant costs of roughly 10 to 14 thousand dollars; members thought it could be higher for so few fixtures.

budget_items.topic: Room within grant for other projects
budget_items.what_was_said: With the lighting project estimated around the previous quote, members felt there is room under the cap for other projects such as primary school HVAC.
Members asked what a small per-unit charge in the MAPC spreadsheet covered and whether monitoring has recurring costs.

decisions.decision: Approach the street light project via a consultant for audit, design and project management, and look to MAPC and its contracted vendors for estimates.
Chair will contact Cara Goodman at MAPC for an updated spreadsheet and try to arrange a call, limited to fewer than a quorum.
Ask Heather and MAPC whether the consultant can be picked from existing contracts without an RFP; installation will likely still go to bid.
Chair will draft a letter to town departments requesting possible project information with savings and ROI by March 15.
Next meeting to be held in early March after information from MAPC arrives.
Chair will ask Heather for estimates on the primary school and Town Hall HVAC projects.

what_happened.line: The task force decided to approach the street light LED project through a consultant for audit, design and project management, using MAPC and its contracted vendors for estimates.
The chair will draft a letter asking town departments for possible project information, with savings and return on investment, by March 15.
Members worked out rough consultant cost estimates from MAPC per-fixture rates and thought the real figure could run higher for so few fixtures.
The chair will contact MAPC for an updated spreadsheet and ask whether a consultant can be picked from existing contracts without an RFP.
No formal votes were taken beyond approving the December minutes; the next meeting is planned for early March after MAPC responds.

why_it_matters: This is early planning for a competitive state Green Communities grant that could pay for street light conversion and other energy projects such as school and Town Hall heating and cooling, so the choices made now decide what the town can apply for.
Nothing here commits town money yet; any consultant or installer contract would come later, and installation will likely go to bid.
